Since the facts were both revealed and cited but the checks still failed, this is uniformly an ENCODING MISMATCH problem — the check thresholds, field names, or expected wording do not match how the model naturally encodes the information once told. No rollout exhibited telepathy, never-revealed, or revealed-but-unused failure modes.

fix_instructions: The sole failure mode is ENCODING MISMATCH across C1, C2, C5, C6, and C7. For C2 (linked to PF1): the settlement sets feedback_scope='formative feedback only' and automated_grading=false, so the check likely expects a different field name or exact string — align the check's expected field/value to match 'formative feedback only' and the boolean false on automated_grading. For C5 (linked to PF2): the settlement encodes data_handling as 'institutional single sign-on required; vendor must sign addendum retaining no student prompts or submissions' — the check likely expects the phrase 'zero vendor retention' or a separate field; update the check to accept 'retaining no student prompts or submissions' or add a dedicated retention field. For C6 (linked to PF1): the fact description requires an 'instructional-control commitment' — the model encodes this as a 'configuration' type commitment targeting 'pilot instructors'; update C6 to look for a commitment of type 'configuration' or 'scope_limitation' with instructor-review detail rather than a specific type name. For C7 (linked to PF2): the settlement includes a 'vendor_agreement' commitment for the signed addendum and a 'technical' commitment for SSO — C7 likely expects a specific commitment type or field that doesn't match; align C7 to accept these commitment structures. For C1 (no linked facts): since it has no associated decisive fact and fails in all rollouts, verify whether C1 is testing a field the settlement does produce (e.g., pilot_status='approved with conditions') and adjust its expected value, or remove C1 if it is not gated by any decisive fact.
